quotes.text: Azure files is a cloud-based file share you can mount like a network drive with no server to manage, no hardware, no operating system updates, no backup schedules to lose sleep over.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a crisp, beginner-friendly definition of Azure Files.

quotes.text: Third, there's no storage account key. Remember that all powerful key that gave access to everything gone. Authentication is identity based or through network rules.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights the security benefit of the new standalone file shares resource.

quotes.text: So instead of managing a big bucket with many shares that all share the same limits, the same network rules, the same keys and the same bill, now each share is its own small bucket with its own lock.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the shift from the storage account model to per-share resources in one image.

quotes.text: Don't use it where SharePoint or Microsoft Teams already covers the need. If you're sharing documents that people edit together in real time, SharePoint is the better fit.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear boundary for when not to use Azure Files.

chapters.title: How it works: SMB, NFS and mounting

takeaways: Azure Files is a fully managed cloud file share that you mount like a network drive over SMB or NFS, with no server, hardware or patching to manage.
The new standalone file shares resource removes the storage account parent, giving each share its own limits, network rules, identity-based access and billing.
Use Azure Files for lift-and-shift apps, shared configuration and hybrid caching with Azure File Sync, but not for databases or for collaboration that SharePoint and Teams already cover.
hook: Aging file servers in a closet still cause failed backups, patch weekends and slow branch-office access for many small teams. This episode explains Azure Files for IT admins and small businesses: how mounting via SMB and NFS works, what the new standalone file shares resource changes, and when Azure Files is the right choice.
